Header: Digitaria abyssinica . Sangari (Kiswahili), Ombugu (Luo), Thangari (Kikuyu), Ekenyambi (Ekegusii)

Prevention: Only use certified seed to avoid introduction through contamination
Practice zero tillage in infested fields where possible, to prevent spread of the weed
Restrict movement of seeds and fragmented rhizomes to uninfested area through cultivation implements (clean after use) and runoff water
Practice crop rotation with legumineous crops, cassava, cotton and other perrenial crops
Plant cover crops such as beans, sweet potatoes, pumpkins and
Dolichos lablab to prevent spread and suppress the weed
Monitoring: Perennial grass with long, slender, branching rhizomes which form a dense mat beneath the soil surface.
Leaves flat bluish- green colour, up to 15 cm long and 2-8 mm wide.
Inflorescences branched with 2 to 25 upwardly pointing, 2-11cm long flower heads ('branches')
Check for the presence of rhizomes in the fields by digging upto 20 cm.
Monitor spread from fallow land or hedges
Monitor for young seedlings before they establish and mature.
Leaves bare a conspicuous membranous legule at the junction of leaf sheath and blade
Direct Control: Tillage with forked hoe; ensure complete removal of rhizomes
Mechanical tillage with tractor to expose rhizomes on the soil surface to facilitate desiccation
Intense use of field by poultry may reduce infestation
Glyphosate (20mL per litre of water), a systemic herbicide, to eradicate couch grass.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Prolific growth of annual broad-leaved weeds occur where
D. abyssinica has been controlled with glyphosate.
